'''Naresh Dadhich''' (1 September 1944 – 6 November 2025) was an Indian [[theoretical physics|theoretical physicist]] at [[IUCAA|Inter-University Center for Astronomy and Astrophysics]] (IUCAA). He was also the director of IUCAA until 31 August 2009. Dadhich held the M.A. Ansari Chair in Theoretical Physics at Centre for Theoretical Physics, [[Jamia Millia Islamia]], Delhi from 2012 to 2016.<ref name=naresh@ctp>{{cite web|last=Dadhich|first=Naresh|title=Naresh Dadhich @ CTP, JMI.|url=http://www.ctp-jamia.res.in/people/nkd.html|work=CTP, JMI Website|publisher=CTP, Jamia Millia Islamia}}</ref>

Dadhich became the director of IUCAA in July 2003.<ref name="narlikar_succession">{{cite news | first=R. | last= Ramachandran| title= Narlikar's successor | date=2003-05-10 | work=[[The Hindu]] | url=http://www.frontlineonnet.com/fl2010/stories/20030523007213400.htm|access-date=2008-03-17}}</ref> In 2012, he was a visiting faculty member at the [[University of KwaZulu-Natal]] at Durban, South Africa<ref>{{cite web|title=ACRU People|url=http://www.acru.ukzn.ac.za/visitors.html|publisher=Astrophysics and Cosmology research unit, University of Kwazulu-Natal|access-date=16 January 2012|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120227175156/http://www.acru.ukzn.ac.za/visitors.html|archive-date=27 February 2012}}</ref> and also worked with gravity research groups in [[Portsmouth|Portsmouth, United Kingdom]] and [[Bilbao|Bilbao, Spain]].

His specialties included classical and [[quantum gravity]] and [[Astrophysics|relativistic astrophysics]]. Along with his colleagues he published over 100 scientific papers and also supervised several [[PhD]] students.

Dadhich died on 6 November 2025, at the age of 81<ref>{{cite news |title=Prof Naresh Dadhich, former director IUCAA, passes away in Beijing |url=https://indianexpress.com/article/cities/pune/prof-naresh-dadhich-former-director-iucaa-passes-away-in-beijing-10350374/ |access-date=6 November 2025 |publisher=The Indian Express |date=6 November 2025}}</ref> in Beijing, China, where he was on an academic visit.
